Routing notes:
- Option C (“regional office” or similar) is invalid for these requests; do not select it.
- Valid choices observed are A (standard queue) and B (priority desk).
- Route explicitly urgent or repeatedly followed-up requests to B: “asking twice already,” “second attempt,” or “before end of day.”
- “No rush” and routine wording (“same as last month,” “confirm receipt”) suggest A.
- Large requests may warrant B when urgency or impact is also indicated; size alone has not been validated as sufficient.
- Region (north, south, east), request type (refund, shipment, claim), sender department, and regional-office wording do not establish a separate routing option.

Routing notes:
- Options A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and C (regional office) can all be valid; the earlier rule that C is always invalid is contradicted by recent outcomes.
- A is supported for routine, low-impact requests: “No rush, but please confirm receipt” (refunds) and possibly similar standard cases.
- B is supported by at least one “Second attempt, the first form bounced” invoice, but this is not universally sufficient: the same wording on a shipment was rejected with B.
- Urgency alone is not reliably mapped to B: “before end of day” was rejected with B.
- “Came in through the regional office” does not itself determine routing: accepted as A for refunds, but A was rejected for a north-region claim.
- “Paperwork was scanned, not typed” is a special-case signal; A was rejected for both a claim and a large invoice.
- Request type and contextual combinations matter. Claims (especially north-region claims), scanned paperwork, and some shipment/invoice cases may require C or another nonstandard route. Exact C outcomes are not yet observed, so do not assert a deterministic mapping.
- Region, sender department, and request size alone remain insufficient. Treat urgency, prior attempts, intake channel, paperwork format, request type, and their combinations as routing signals; use confirmed examples cautiously.

Routing notes:
- A, B, and C can all be valid; no option is universally determined by a single signal.
- A is supported for routine refunds: low-impact “No rush, but please confirm receipt,” south-region large refund with “before end of day,” and north-region small refund after a bounced first form.
- A is not reliable for shipments: east-region small shipment with “before end of day” was rejected. Prior evidence also rejected A for north-region claims and scanned paperwork.
- B has limited support: one invoice with “Second attempt, the first form bounced.” It was rejected for a shipment and for a south-region large refund mentioning repeated follow-up. Do not treat urgency or prior attempts alone as sufficient.
- C is now confirmed valid for at least one south-region small claim with “before end of day.” However, C was rejected for north-region large refund, north-region large claim, and both large and small north-region shipments. Earlier evidence also rejected C in other cases; do not assume regional origin implies C.
- Request type, region, size, intake channel, paperwork format, urgency, prior attempts, and their combinations matter. Claims may sometimes require C, but north-region status alone does not establish that; a north-region claim routed to C was rejected.
- “Came in through the regional office” is not determinative: it was accepted as A for some refunds, while A was rejected for a north-region claim.
- “Paperwork was scanned, not typed” remains a strong special-case signal against A (claim and large invoice examples).
- Region, sender department, and size alone remain insufficient. Prefer confirmed analogies, and treat every inferred mapping as tentative until the exact combination is observed.

Routing notes:
- No option is universally determined by one signal; request type, region, size, channel, paperwork, urgency, prior attempts, and their combinations matter. Prefer exact confirmed analogies and keep inferences tentative.
- A is supported for several refunds: routine/low-impact refunds, south large refund with “before end of day,” north small refunds via regional office, north small refund after a bounced first form, and east small refund with repeated follow-up.
- A is unreliable for shipments, claims, and invoices: rejected for east small shipment with urgency, north claims, scanned paperwork, and east large invoice with urgency.
- B has limited but expanded support: accepted for a north-region large shipment via the regional office. Earlier evidence supports B for one invoice with a bounced first form, but it was rejected for another shipment and a south large refund with repeated follow-up. Do not infer B from urgency, size, or prior attempts alone.
- C is confirmed for south claims with urgency (both small and large) and for a south large claim with scanned paperwork. It is rejected for east small claim with urgency, north small claim with “no rush,” north large refund/claim, and north large or small shipments. North-region status alone does not imply C.
- “Came in through the regional office” is not determinative: accepted as A for north small refunds, B for a north large shipment, and previously A for some refunds; it does not establish one route.
- Scanned rather than typed paperwork remains a strong signal against A and supports C in confirmed claim examples, but do not generalize beyond matching request/region/size combinations.
- Option D is invalid in the observed north small shipment case; treat D as unsupported unless directly validated.

Routing notes:
- No option is determined by a single signal. Match request type, region, size, urgency, paperwork, channel, prior attempts, and combinations; prefer exact confirmed analogies and keep inferences tentative.
- A is supported for routine/low-impact refunds, south large refunds with urgency, north small refunds via regional office or after a bounced first form, east small refunds with repeated follow-up, and east large refunds with a missing-information note.
- A is rejected for several shipments, claims, and invoices: east small urgent shipment, north claims, scanned paperwork, east large urgent invoice, east large invoice with “same as last month,” and south small invoice with repeated follow-up. Do not generalize rejection beyond matching patterns.
- B is confirmed for north large shipments (including no-rush), north small urgent invoices, and north small claims with a missing-information note. Earlier evidence also supports B for one invoice after a bounced first form. B was rejected for an east large claim with repeated follow-up, another shipment, and a south large refund with repeated follow-up. Do not infer B from urgency, size, or prior attempts alone.
- C is confirmed for south claims: small/no rush, small or large urgent, and large with scanned paperwork. It is rejected for east claims (small urgent and large, including “same as last month” or repeated follow-up), north claims, north shipments, and north large refunds. South-region status alone does not imply C.
- Regional-office intake is not determinative: observed valid routes include A (north small refunds), B (north large shipment), and C (south claims).
- Scanned paperwork strongly disfavors A and supports C in matching claim examples; avoid broader generalization.
- D remains unsupported; invalid in the observed north small shipment case.

Routing notes:
- No option is determined by one signal. Match request type, region, size, urgency, paperwork, channel, prior attempts, and their combinations. Prefer exact confirmed analogies; keep inferences tentative.
- A is confirmed for routine/low-impact refunds: south large refunds with urgency, repeated follow-up, or a bounced first form; south small refunds with no rush or missing-information language; north small refunds via regional office or after a bounced first form; east small refunds with repeated follow-up or missing-information language.
- A is rejected for east large invoices via regional office, east small shipments via regional office, south small shipments with repeated follow-up, east small urgent shipments, north claims, scanned paperwork, east large urgent invoices, east large invoices saying “same as last month,” and south small invoices with repeated follow-up. Do not generalize rejection beyond matching patterns.
- B is confirmed for north large shipments (including no-rush), north small urgent or scanned-paperwork invoices, north small claims with a missing-information note, and east small invoices with repeated follow-up. Earlier evidence also supports B for one invoice after a bounced first form. B was rejected for an east large claim with repeated follow-up, another shipment, and a south large refund with repeated follow-up. Do not infer B from urgency, size, or prior attempts alone.
- C is confirmed for south claims: small/no rush, small or large urgent, and large with scanned paperwork. It is rejected for east claims, north claims, north shipments, and north large refunds. South-region status alone does not imply C.
- Regional-office intake is not determinative: valid routes include A (north small refunds), B (north large shipment), and C (south claims), while A is rejected for the observed east large invoice and east small shipment.
- Scanned paperwork strongly disfavors A and supports C for matching claims; it supported B in the observed north small invoice. Avoid broader generalization.
- D remains unsupported; invalid in the observed north small shipment case.
